rebeccah: Heads up 1 onboarding lab produced confusing output: Python SDK bubbled a plain RuntimeError for an expired key and a second flow returned only a raw 429 status with no body, so sample-app showed a full traceback to the user.

eli: Oof. We need a compact, machine- and human-friendly contract that SDKs parse into typed exceptions. Customers shouldn't have to parse strings.

noor: Proposal (server JSON body): `{\n  \"error_id\": \"auth.token_expired\",\n  \"status_code\": 401,\n  \"message\": \"API key expired\",\n  \"action\": \"reauth\",\n  \"retry_after_seconds\": null,\n  \"transient\": false,\n  \"docs\": \"https://docs.redwood.ai/errors#auth.token_expired\"\n}`. For rate limits `transient`=true and `retry_after_seconds` populated from header when available.

frank: I like `error_id` instead of `code` because it reads like a stable enum string we can document. Also `transient` helps UIs pick whether to show "try again" vs "contact support".

kim: SDK strategy: add new typed exceptions that subclass existing ones (so code catching HTTPError/RuntimeError keeps working). E.g. `RedwoodError` <- `RedwoodAuthError`, `RedwoodRateLimitError`, `RedwoodClientError`, `RedwoodServerError`. Each exception should expose attributes: `error_id` (str), `status_code` (int), `retry_after_seconds` (int|None), `transient` (bool), `raw_body` (str|None).

rebeccah: For backwards compatibility, if the server returns no JSON body we fall back to current behavior but set `status_code` from the response. Also emit a non-fatal deprecation log when legacy catch-all codepaths are hit so we can surface common regressions.

eli: Sample app suggestion (py): ```py
try:
    r = client.generate(req)
except RedwoodRateLimitError as e:
    wait = e.retry_after_seconds or 1
    show_banner(f"Service busy 1 try again in {wait}s")
    sleep(wait)
    retry()
except RedwoodAuthError:
    show_modal("Session expired 1 please sign in again")
except Exception as e:
    # fallback: keep user-facing copy concise, opt-in debug modal for devs
    show_banner("Service temporarily unavailable 1 try again")
    if os.getenv('REDWOOD_DEBUG'):
        show_debug(e.raw_body or str(e))
```

noor: I want an explicit migration path: 1) server adds JSON body and headers, 2) SDKs parse and raise typed exceptions, 3) sample-apps updated to catch typed exceptions, 4) docs + changelog + support snippets.

frank: CI: Add sample-app unit tests that mock 401/429 with JSON body and assert the UI shows friendly copy and the SDK exceptions expose attributes. We'll gate the SDK PRs with these tests.

kim: Implementation detail: keep `error_id` stable (namespace like `auth.*`, `rate.*`, `quota.*`) and avoid embedding freeform messages in `error_id`. Freeform goes in `message`. Also include a short `docs` URL for quick copy/paste.

rebeccah: Ops ask: include a short support-friendly paste for common cases so support can reply quickly. Example: "If you see auth.token_expired (401), ask user to re-authenticate; if rate.limit_exceeded (429), recommend retry with exponential backoff and include the `retry_after_seconds` if present."

ops-bot: CI: sample-apps/error-handling-tests passed on branch error-contracts (build #1306) :white_check_mark:

eli: Naming nit: prefer `status_code` (explicit) + `retry_after_seconds` (clear unit). Good to be explicit here.

noor: Also add a tiny SDK convenience: `e.is_retryable()` method that returns bool based on `transient` and `retry_after_seconds` so app code doesn't replicate logic.

kim: Good idea. We'll implement that in py/js/go. Also add short examples in onboarding quickstart that show recommended handling.

rebeccah: Owners: noor (RFC + server schema), kim (SDK changes), frank (sample-app CI + UI), eli (support paste + docs snippet). ETA: RFC + minimal PRs Weds.

eli: Thanks all. Let's avoid throwing stack traces to end users by default. Small DX win with big reduction in support noise. :sparkles:
